Description: Move await into branches where actually used to avoid blocking unused code paths
Do: Move await operations into branches where they're needed
Don't: Await at top of function blocking all branches
Code Example Good: if (skip) return { skipped: true }; const data = await fetch()
Code Example Bad: const data = await fetch(); if (skip) return { skipped: true }

Description: Execute independent async operations concurrently using Promise.all()
Do: Use Promise.all() for independent operations
Don't: Sequential await for independent operations
Code Example Bad: const user = await fetchUser(); const posts = await fetchPosts()

Description: Use better-all for operations with partial dependencies to maximize parallelism
Do: Use better-all to start each task at earliest possible moment
Don't: Wait for unrelated data before starting dependent fetch
Code Example Good: await all({ user() {}, config() {}, profile() { return fetch((await this.$.user).id) } })
Code Example Bad: const [user, config] = await Promise.all([...]); const profile = await fetchProfile(user.id)

Description: In API routes start independent operations immediately even if not awaited yet
Do: Start promises early and await late
Don't: Sequential awaits in API handlers
Code Example Good: const sessionP = auth(); const configP = fetchConfig(); const session = await sessionP
Code Example Bad: const session = await auth(); const config = await fetchConfig()

Description: Use Suspense to show wrapper UI faster while data loads
Do: Wrap async components in Suspense boundaries
Don't: Await data blocking entire page render
Code Example Bad: const data = await fetchData(); return <DataDisplay data={data} />

Description: Import directly from source files instead of barrel files to avoid loading unused modules
Do: Import directly from source path
Don't: Import from barrel/index files

Description: Use next/dynamic to lazy-load large components not needed on initial render
Do: Use dynamic() for heavy components
Don't: Import heavy components at top level
Code Example Good: const Monaco = dynamic(() => import('./monaco'), { ssr: false })

Description: Load analytics and logging after hydration since they don't block interaction
Do: Load non-critical scripts after hydration
Don't: Include analytics in main bundle
Code Example Good: const Analytics = dynamic(() => import('@vercel/analytics'), { ssr: false })

Description: Load large data or modules only when a feature is activated
Do: Dynamic import when feature enabled
Don't: Import large modules unconditionally

Description: Preload heavy bundles on hover/focus before they're needed
Do: Preload on user intent signals
Don't: Load only on click

Description: Use React.cache() for server-side request deduplication within single request
Do: Wrap data fetchers with cache()
Don't: Fetch same data multiple times in tree
Code Example Good: export const getUser = cache(async () => await db.user.find())
Code Example Bad: export async function getUser() { return await db.user.find() }

Description: Use LRU cache for data shared across sequential requests
Do: Use LRU for cross-request caching
Don't: Refetch same data on every request
Code Example Good: const cache = new LRUCache({ max: 1000, ttl: 5*60*1000 })

Description: Only pass fields that client actually uses across RSC boundaries
Do: Pass only needed fields to client components
Don't: Pass entire objects to client

Description: Restructure components to parallelize data fetching in RSC
Do: Use component composition for parallel fetches
Don't: Sequential fetches in parent component

Description: Use Next.js after() to schedule work after response is sent
Do: Use after() for logging/analytics
Don't: Block response for non-critical operations

Description: Use SWR for automatic request deduplication and caching
Do: Use useSWR for client data fetching
Don't: Manual fetch in useEffect

Description: Share global event listeners across component instances
Do: Use useSWRSubscription for shared listeners
Don't: Register listener per component instance

Description: Don't subscribe to state only used in callbacks
Do: Read state on-demand in callbacks
Don't: Subscribe to state used only in handlers
Code Example Good: const handleClick = () => { const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search) }
Code Example Bad: const params = useSearchParams(); const handleClick = () => { params.get('ref') }

Description: Extract expensive work into memoized components for early returns
Do: Extract to memo() components; not needed with React Compiler
Don't: Compute expensive values before early return
Code Example Good: const UserAvatar = memo(({ user }) => ...); if (loading) return <Skeleton />
Code Example Bad: const avatar = useMemo(() => compute(user)); if (loading) return <Skeleton />

Description: Specify primitive dependencies instead of objects in effects
Do: Use primitive values in dependency arrays
Don't: Use object references as dependencies

Description: Subscribe to derived booleans instead of continuous values
Do: Use derived boolean state
Don't: Subscribe to continuous values
Code Example Bad: const width = useWindowWidth(); const isMobile = width < 768

Description: Use functional setState updates for stable callbacks and no stale closures
Do: Use functional form: setState(curr => ...)
Don't: Reference state directly in setState

Description: Pass function to useState for expensive initial values
Do: Use function form for expensive init
Don't: Compute expensive value directly

Description: Mark frequent non-urgent state updates as transitions
Do: Use startTransition for non-urgent updates
Don't: Block UI on every state change

Description: Wrap SVG in div and animate wrapper for hardware acceleration
Do: Animate div wrapper around SVG
Don't: Animate SVG element directly

Description: Apply content-visibility: auto to defer off-screen rendering
Do: Use content-visibility for long lists
Don't: Render all list items immediately

Description: Extract static JSX outside components to avoid re-creation
Do: Hoist static elements to module scope; not needed with React Compiler
Don't: Create static elements inside components
Code Example Good: const skeleton = <div class='animate-pulse' />; function C() { return skeleton }

Description: Use inline script to set client-only data before hydration
Do: Inject sync script for client-only values
Don't: Use useEffect causing flash

Description: Use ternary instead of && when condition can be 0 or NaN
Do: Use explicit ternary for conditionals
Don't: Use && with potentially falsy numbers

Description: Use Activity component to preserve state/DOM for toggled components
Do: Use Activity for expensive toggle components
Don't: Unmount/remount on visibility toggle

Description: Group CSS changes via classes or cssText to minimize reflows
Do: Use class toggle or cssText
Don't: Change styles one property at a time

Description: Use toSorted() instead of sort() to avoid mutating arrays
Do: Use toSorted() for immutability
Don't: Mutate arrays with sort()

Description: Store callbacks in refs for stable effect subscriptions
Do: Use useEffectEvent for stable handlers
Don't: Re-subscribe on every callback change

Description: Read the latest callback inside an effect with useEffectEvent so it does not re-run when the callback changes
Do: Wrap the callback in useEffectEvent and call it from the effect
Don't: Add the changing callback to the effect dependencies
Code Example Good: const onSearchEvent = useEffectEvent(onSearch); useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => onSearchEvent(query), 300); return () => clearTimeout(t) }, [query])
Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => onSearch(query), 300); return () => clearTimeout(t) }, [query, onSearch]) // re-runs when onSearch changes

Issue: Effect Events Stay Out of Dependencies
Description: An Effect Event has a new identity every render, so listing it as a dependency re-runs the effect every render
Do: Call the Effect Event inside the effect and leave it out of the dependency array
Don't: Put the useEffectEvent function in the dependency array
Code Example Good: const onConnected = useEffectEvent(cb); useEffect(() => { conn.on('connected', onConnected) }, [roomId])
Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => { conn.on('connected', onConnected) }, [roomId, onConnected]) // re-runs every render

Keywords: init once module guard effect mount strict mode
Description: App-wide setup in useEffect([]) re-runs on remount and twice in dev
Do: Use a module-level guard or top-level init for once-per-load work
Don't: Run once-per-load setup inside a component effect
Code Example Good: let didInit = false; useEffect(() => { if (didInit) return; didInit = true; init() }, [])
Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => { loadFromStorage(); checkAuthToken() }, []) // re-runs on remount

Description: Check a cheap synchronous condition before awaiting a flag or remote value
Do: Test the local condition first, then await the flag inside it
Don't: Await the flag first and test the cheap condition afterwards
Code Example Good: if (someCondition) { const flag = await getFlag(); if (flag) { /* ... */ } }
Code Example Bad: const flag = await getFlag(); if (flag && someCondition) { /* ... */ }

Keywords: analyzable path dynamic import bundler glob
Description: Hidden or over-dynamic import and file paths make the bundler include a broad set of files
Do: Use an explicit map of allowed modules or literal paths
Don't: Compose import or file paths from variables the bundler cannot resolve
Code Example Good: const PAGES = { home: () => import('./pages/home'), settings: () => import('./pages/settings') }; await PAGES[name]()
Code Example Bad: await import(PAGE_MODULES[pageName]) // path hidden in a variable

Description: Prefix storage keys with a version, store only the fields needed, and wrap access in try/catch
Do: Save a minimal object under a versioned key and handle thrown errors
Don't: Store whole objects under an unversioned key without error handling

Description: Browsers wait for touch and wheel listeners to check preventDefault, which delays scrolling
Do: Pass { passive: true } on touch and wheel listeners that never call preventDefault
Don't: Add touch or wheel listeners without passive when preventDefault is not needed

Description: Values that differ between server and client on purpose (dates, locale formatting) warn on hydration
Do: Add suppressHydrationWarning to the element holding the expected mismatch only
Don't: Suppress the warning on large subtrees or on unexpected mismatches

Keywords: preconnect preload prefetchdns preinit resource hints
Description: React DOM preload, preconnect and preinit APIs start fetching critical resources early, including from server components
Do: Call preconnect or preload for known third-party origins, fonts and styles
Don't: Wait for the browser to discover critical resources late
Code Example Bad: // no hint, connection opened only when first fetch runs

Description: Script tags without defer or async block HTML parsing and delay first paint
Do: Use defer for DOM-dependent scripts and async for independent ones like analytics
Don't: Ship plain script tags in the head

Description: Excess decimal places in SVG paths add file size with no visible gain
Do: Reduce coordinate precision (about 1 decimal for typical icons) with SVGO
Don't: Keep exported 6-digit coordinates

Description: useTransition provides isPending and manages the transition, replacing a hand-rolled loading flag
Do: Wrap the async update in startTransition and read isPending
Don't: Keep a manual isLoading useState toggled around the await
Code Example Good: const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition(); startTransition(async () => { setResults(await fetchResults(v)) })
Code Example Bad: setIsLoading(true); const d = await fetchResults(v); setResults(d); setIsLoading(false)

Keywords: derived state effect setstate render redundant
Description: A value computable from props or state should be computed during render, not stored and synced in an effect
Do: Compute the value inline in the component body
Don't: Store derived values in state and update them in useEffect

Description: A non-primitive default parameter creates a new value each render and defeats memo
Do: Extract the default array, object or function to a module constant (unneeded with React Compiler)
Don't: Inline a non-primitive default in a memoized component signature
Code Example Good: const NOOP = () => {}; const Avatar = memo(({ onClick = NOOP }) => null)

Keywords: event handler effect state submit side effect
Description: A side effect caused by a user action belongs in that event handler, not in state plus an effect
Do: Run the effect directly in the click or submit handler
Don't: Set a flag in state and react to it in useEffect

Description: A component defined inside another gets a new type every render and remounts, losing state and DOM
Do: Define components at module level and pass props
Don't: Declare components inside a component to reach its variables
Code Example Good: function Avatar({ user, theme }) { return } // module level

Description: A cheap expression with a primitive result costs less than useMemo and its dependency check
Do: Compute the boolean, number or string inline
Don't: Wrap a simple logical or arithmetic expression in useMemo
Code Example Bad: const isLoading = useMemo(() => user.isLoading || notifications.isLoading, [user.isLoading, notifications.isLoading])

Description: One hook with independent tasks reruns all of them when any dependency changes
Do: Give each independent computation its own hook and dependencies (measure first; unneeded with React Compiler)
Don't: Combine filtering and sorting in one memo keyed on every input
Code Example Good: const filtered = useMemo(() => products.filter(byCategory), [products, category]); const sorted = useMemo(() => filtered.toSorted(cmp), [filtered, sortOrder])

Description: Keep input responsive by deferring the expensive derived render
Do: Pass the deferred value to the expensive list
Don't: Filter large lists synchronously on every keystroke
Code Example Good: const deferred = useDeferredValue(query); const filtered = useMemo(() => items.filter(m(deferred)), [items, deferred])
Code Example Bad: const filtered = items.filter(item => fuzzyMatch(item, query)) // blocks typing

Keywords: useref transient mouse interval no rerender
Description: Values that change very often and need no render belong in a ref, not state
Do: Store the value in useRef and update the DOM directly
Don't: Put every mousemove or timer tick in useState
Code Example Good: const xRef = useRef(0); onMove = e => { xRef.current = e.clientX; dot.style.transform = `translateX(${e.clientX}px)` }
Code Example Bad: const [lastX, setLastX] = useState(0); onMove = e => setLastX(e.clientX) // renders every move

Keywords: server action auth authorization use server public endpoint
Description: Server Actions are public endpoints; verify auth and authorization inside each one
Do: Check the session and permission at the top of every action
Don't: Assume the calling page already authorized the user
Code Example Good: 'use server'; export async function deleteUser(id) { const s = await verifySession(); if (!s) throw new Error('Unauthorized'); /* ... */ }
Code Example Bad: 'use server'; export async function deleteUser(id) { await db.user.delete({ where: { id } }) }

Description: RSC serialization dedupes by reference, so a transformed copy is sent again
Do: Send the data once and transform it in the client component
Don't: Pass both the array and a toSorted or map copy as props

Keywords: static io hoist module level font route handler og
Description: Reading fonts, logos or config in a route handler runs I/O on every request
Do: Hoist the fetch or file read to module level so it runs once
Don't: Load static assets inside the request handler
Code Example Good: const fontData = fetch(new URL('./Inter.ttf', import.meta.url)).then(r => r.arrayBuffer())
Code Example Bad: export async function GET() { const font = await fetch(new URL('./Inter.ttf', import.meta.url)) }

Keywords: module state shared request ssr concurrency leak
Description: Mutable module-level variables are process-wide on the server, so concurrent requests overwrite each other
Do: Pass request data through props, React.cache or request context
Don't: Assign request-scoped data to a module-level variable
Code Example Good: const user = await auth(); return <Dashboard user={user} />
Code Example Bad: let currentUser = null; export default async function Page() { currentUser = await auth() }

Keywords: parallel nested fetch chain promise all
Description: Chain dependent fetches inside each item's promise so one slow item does not block the rest
Do: Chain the nested fetch with .then inside the per-item Promise.all
Don't: Await all parents, then start all children
Code Example Bad: const chats = await Promise.all(ids.map(getChat)); const users = await Promise.all(chats.map(c => getUser(c.author)))
